rationale: The compiled artifact faithfully implements the design's route (channel_members→channels→teams→user_teams(role='admin')→users) and correctly adds an auxiliary query to encode the 'same person' constraint (r0.user_id = r4.user_id) that the binding_note requires but that the plain literal route alone cannot express — this is a legitimate use of an auxiliary path to preserve the requested semantic equality, not a fabricated addition. All facts (Robert Walsh and Morgan Freeman as Test Workspace admins; Priya and Łukasz as ordinary-role #core-infra members) exist verbatim in the base seed, so no seed edits were needed and no environment-mutation requirement applies. computed_matches/computed_focal_negatives are empty and checks.errors is empty, consistent with the absence resolution: no #core-infra channel_members row's own user_id carries an admin-role user_teams row on Test Workspace. The negative_referents set is well-chosen and path-derived (three of Walsh's non-#core-infra channel memberships showing wrong-channel failure, plus Priya/Łukasz showing wrong-role failure), giving genuine, non-hint-revealing coverage of the absence claim. Written/change attributes remain empty, matching the absent obligation with no fabricated literal values. The actor (a documented member of both Test Workspace and #core-infra) has real, non-hidden API access via users.list/users.info and conversations.members to establish the absence, and the task remains a supported state-changing action (conversations.kick) whose correct behavior is to find no valid target. This matches the earlier design review's conclusion and introduces no new defects at compilation time.
